A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, datasets and retained experiments. Text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable. The expanded and reorganized material in v2 supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original vision and NLP experiments on expert training duration, model merging, LoRA rank, data difficulty, MoErging and early stopping.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds evaluations of further merging methods and models, randomized memorization experiments, interference analyses and NLP early stopping.

M1.justification: Section 5.2 adds a T5 early-stopping procedure using constant learning rates, validation intervals/patiences of (100, 5) or (50, 3), and best-validation-checkpoint selection. The existing vision warm-up/adaptive-decay strategy and MoErging procedure are retained; the added vision pseudocode primarily documents the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight vision classification datasets and seven NLP tasks. The additional ViT, BERT and T5 evaluations reuse this coverage, and MoErging remains in Appendix K. Randomly withholding examples introduces experimental controls within existing datasets.

E2.justification: v2 adds Iso-C, Iso-CTS and TSV-M to the evaluated merging methods in Figures 1–2. DARE also joins the NLP comparisons, where v1 Figure 2 evaluated only Average, Task Arithmetic and TIES, and the forgotten-example comparison expands to include DARE.

E3.justification: v2 adds ViT-L-14, BERT-Base, T5-Large and T5-3B configurations, language early-stopping protocols, and new memorization/interference measurements. Its randomized memorization experiment withholds 90 examples per training run across difficulty groups. The original dataset splits and raw-accuracy evaluation remain.

E4.justification: Section 4 and Appendices D–I add randomized example-inclusion analyses, early-versus-late prediction diagnostics, parameter-interference measurements, per-task breakdowns and model-scale sensitivity. These substantially extend the mechanism and generality checks. Existing pruning, LoRA-rank and MoErging analyses are retained, including material relocated to appendices.

E5.justification: Beyond v1's mean/standard-deviation reporting, v2 adds inclusion-conditioned memorization estimation using 40 seeded models per dataset and Pearson correlations with significance tests in Appendix H. Appendix I specifies aggregation across task pairs and seeds. Figure 2 reports three seeds instead of two; the PDFs do not establish how the underlying runs were updated.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for new comparators and model configurations, T5 early stopping, memorization and interference. Table 2 reports 77.0 ± 0.3% TIES accuracy for aggressive T5 early stopping. Retained forgotten-example shares also change, such as Task Arithmetic's hardest-bin share from 28.7% to 28.3%. Table 1's merging means and the MoErging table results are retained.

T1.justification: v2 introduces formal definitions for inclusion-conditioned memorization and parameter-interference diagnostics, including pruned support sets and a zero-mean assumption for its variance measure. These are limited formal additions supporting empirical analyses; no new theorem or proof is developed, and the original merging, LoRA and MoErging mathematics remain.

C1.justification: The central claims about harmful expert overtraining, difficult-example memorization and beneficial early stopping remain. v2 explicitly extends the headline scope across model scales and asserts a causal role for negative parameter interference. MoErging is reframed as an appendix extension while its substantive claim is retained.

C2.justification: v2 develops the previously hypothesized memorization mechanism into a stronger causal account involving idiosyncratic updates and parameter interference. It presents early stopping as a general principle and suggests one plateau-stage checkpoint may suffice. The conclusion removes v1's explicit limitations concerning small models, restricted method coverage and already-published adapters.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public-code access statement, early-stopping pseudocode and the previously unspecified 1e-7 stopping threshold. It supplies additional comparator tuning grids, model settings and analysis procedures. Appendix B also clarifies that tuning occurs separately for every duration and seed; this documents existing evaluation rather than establishing a changed protocol.

R1.justification: v2 adds SVD-merging references, work on specialized fine-tuning procedures, and Zhou et al.'s task-vector/gradient analysis. Section 6 explains how studying standard fine-tuning complements these approaches, while two broad MoE-upcycling references disappear. The central positioning around expert training duration and data difficulty remains.

P1.justification: The title, introduction, mechanism narrative, early-stopping discussion, related work and conclusion are substantially revised. LoRA-rank analysis moves to Appendix G, and MoErging material is consolidated in Appendix K. Section 4 is organized around three observations, and Section 5 separates vision and language strategies.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout and substantially expands its displays. Figure 2 gains a model-scale panel, Table 1 gains an Experts column and result highlighting, and the forgotten-example display gains DARE. New diagnostic figures, tables and pseudocode accompany relocated rank/MoErging displays. Reversed FFT/LoRA panel descriptions in v1 captions are corrected.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1's largely indirect memorization evidence through randomized example inclusion, broader comparator/model validation and NLP early-stopping experiments. Added code-access information and implementation detail improve reproducibility. The stronger causal account remains imperfect: Appendix I labels an uncentered second moment as variance, gives inconsistent pruning-threshold definitions, and states a 60-fold increase where Table 4 implies about 604-fold. These weaknesses limit the mechanism interpretation but do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support and practical usefulness.
